attempted: Hardcoding the new line's indent to "\n " instead of deriving it from the array (only cosmetic, weak violation)
Fixing only `append` and leaving `insert`/`extend`/`+=` broken (caught by R3 probe cases)
Dropping the trailing comment when appending (caught by the R6 exact-layout regression cases)
Fixing the newline placement but scoping the ",," guard to `pos < length` only (insert middle), leaving append broken

Guarding the double-comma only for whitespace groups, without noticing the new item then *copies* that same comma-bearing indent — leaves leading-comma arrays that end in a dangling comma after a comment still unparseable (this is the counterexample)

rounds.detail: Array.insert starts a new line when the previous group ends in a comment and suppresses the duplicate comma on a stranded whitespace group, but still reuses that stranded group's comma-bearing indent for the new item, so appending to a leading-comma array that has both a trailing comment and a dangling trailing comma emits ", ,99" and remains unparseable.

Sanitize by stripping underscores/whitespace before int() (accept-and-normalize instead of reject) — caught by every rejection case.
Pre-validate with `extracted.isalnum()` alone — caught by the Arabic-Indic/fullwidth digit case (they are alnum).

Pre-validate with `extracted.isascii() and extracted.isalnum()` and let int() reject the remaining letters — PASSES the whole oracle, but int(s, 16) accepts a `0x`/`0X` base prefix, so `\u0x41` still decodes to "A".
rounds.detail: Validates escape digits with `extracted.isascii() and extracted.isalnum()` and relies on int() to reject non-hex letters, which still accepts the `0x`/`0X` base prefix int() honours for base 16, so `\u0x41` and `\U0x000041` decode to "A".
